title: Executor integration of the native quantised Vulkan dot product
scope: Blueprint step 04. Routes a real Deep2 quantised projection through the verified kernel via a dedicated dispatcher, proves via counters that the GPU actually ran, records fallback authority, exercises tiled dispatch, and separates cold-start from steady-state timing. All weights are real bytes from real GGUF files.

integration.executor_wiring: src/modelgenie/ModelGenieExecutor.cpp :: DotBlocked() now calls RawrXD::Deep2::QuantDot::DotBlocked for the Q4_K / Q6_K branch and returns whether the GPU actually ran.
design_rules: The GPU path is never claimed unless ExecuteQuantDot actually ran; dispatches increment either gpu_calls or cpu_calls.
Unsupported shapes and GPU failures fall back to the caller's CPU reference and record the reason in FallbackReason(). There is no silent fallback.
The activation is quantised and interleaved once and reused across every row tile; the packed pointer is advanced per tile so weights are uploaded per tile, not per row.
Cold start is recorded on first Vulkan initialisation and is never averaged into steady-state kernel time; ResetStats() preserves it.

acceptance_requirements.4_tiled_execution: PASS (Exercised on the 8192-row tensor: 2 tiles of 4096 rows.)

requirement_3_fallback.unsupported_shape: in=8224 not a multiple of 256 -> no GPU dispatch, reason 'shape:', CPU reference still correct
requirement_3_fallback.forced_cpu: SetForceCpu(true) -> no GPU dispatch, reason names the hook, CPU reference still correct

requirement_4_tiling.note: 512 rows fit one tile, so tiling is not exercised on this tensor; it is exercised on the 8192-row tensor above.

requirement_5_performance.steady_state_note: single tile, so there is no dispatch after the first; reported as 0.000 rather than fabricated

activation_quantisation_note: Both the GPU kernel and the CPU reference consume the SAME quantised activation built with the Q8_K rule d = amax/127 with per-16 sums, which is identical to the executor's existing QuantizeQ8KGroup and to ggml's Q8_K reference. The comparison therefore isolates kernel arithmetic, not the choice of quantiser. As documented in RAWRXD_DEEP2_GPU_QUANT_DOT_002, this per-256-scaled layout differs from ggml's per-32 fp16 Q8_0 by about 1.6% relative L2; that difference is an intended property of the layout and is kept separate from kernel numerical error.
what_this_establishes: A real Deep2 projection path (Q4_K and Q6_K) invokes the native quantised Vulkan kernel, and the counters prove the GPU ran rather than a CPU fallback.
Full output-vector parity against an independent reference on real weights: cosine 1.0, relative RMSE at most 3.2e-07, max absolute error at most 1.3e-08, all values finite.
Fallback authority: an unsupported shape and a forced CPU path both decline the GPU, record the reason, and still produce correct output.
Tiled dispatch runs multiple dispatches per projection with the activation quantised and uploaded once per tile.
Cold start (about 1.73 s, dominated by Vulkan pipeline creation) is recorded separately from steady-state kernel time, so it is never mistaken for per-token cost.
what_this_does_not_establish: Any TPS figure. Cold start is about 1.73 s per process, and the 61 ms per-call projection latency above is a 8192-row full projection, not a single decoding step. No end-to-end decode throughput is measured here.

End-to-end GPU decode. The full ModelGenieExecutor binary was not linked in this environment because its generated IR headers (ModelExport.generated.hpp, ExecutionIR.generated.hpp and friends) exist only in a model-specific worktree; the call site was verified for type correctness with a dedicated translation unit.
GPU attention, RMSNorm, softmax, V aggregation, or KV-cache primitives.
That the tiled kernel is optimal. It dispatches one invocation per output row with host upload and readback; it is correct, not tuned.
next: Link the full executor once the generated IR headers are available, and capture a real token-level decode trace showing gpu_calls incrementing during inference.
Reduce the cold start: about 1.73 s per process is Vulkan pipeline and descriptor setup, which is amortisation-dependent and will dominate any single-shot measurement.

Move to a multi-invocation-per-row tiling (several rows per invocation) and persistent device buffers before measuring TPS, since the step-02 profile showed 97% of decode time is weight-bandwidth-bound mul_mat.
Implement the remaining primitives (attention, RMSNorm, softmax, V aggregation) before certifying a GPU-resident layer.
